topic: x86-64 Procedure Call Convention and Stack Frame Management
explanation: x86-64 uses a calling convention to manage procedure calls, defining how arguments are passed, return values are handled, and how the stack is used to manage local variables and control flow.  Understanding this convention is crucial for writing efficient and correct systems-level code, as it directly impacts performance and memory usage.  The stack frame, a region on the stack allocated for each procedure, allows for dynamic storage allocation and proper function nesting.

extraction_metadata.source: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)

book: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)
code_example:
; x86-64 System V ABI Stack Frame

; Arguments: RDI, RSI, RDX, RCX, R8, R9
; Return Value: RAX (Caller-saved)

function_name:
    ; PROLOGUE (Frame Setup)
    push rbp        ; Save base pointer
    mov rbp, rsp    ; Establish new frame base

    ; Local Variable Allocation (must align RSP to 16 bytes - 0x10)
    sub rsp, 0x20

    ; Access Arg1 (RDI is at (RBP + 0x10) usually, or used directly)
    mov [rbp - 0x8], rdi ; Store arg1 locally

    ; EPILOGUE (Frame Teardown)
    mov rsp, rbp    ; Deallocate stack space
    pop rbp         ; Restore base pointer
    ret             ; Return to caller (pops RIP)
keywords: x64 calling convention, Stack frame, System V ABI, x86-64 procedure call
